svg.title: STR-500 Cantilever Balcony Structure
svg.text: SLAB EDGE — THICKNESS, ROOT DEPTH AND REINFORCEMENT BY THE ENGINEER
LEVEL +13.20 and the three floors below · 1:20 @ A1 · METRES
External / party wall cut by section, 300 mm —
Single leaf door, swing shown to opening side
Glazed opening — arched head where noted
Element above the cut plane (pergola, slab
1. Layout only. No member size, no slab or footing depth, no
reinforcement and no load appears on this sheet or
anywhere in the STR series. Those are the structural
engineer's, and a column schedule with sizes invented by
an architect is worse than none, because somebody builds
2. The grid, the column coordinates, the spans and the slab
edges are measured from the same geometry the architecture
is drawn from and are exact.
3. A 1.95 m cantilever on a curve, repeated on four levels,
is the single most engineering-sensitive element in this
building. It is drawn at 1:20 for that reason and for no
4. The curve, the span, the projection at every point and the
balustrade line are exact. The slab thickness, the root
depth into the floor behind, the top steel and the
deflection and vibration checks are entirely the
5. Grid line 1 runs along the face the cantilever springs
from. The balcony projects south of it and is unsupported
at its far edge on all four levels.
Layout for the engineer's design — no member sizes, no reinforcement, no loads. Not for construction.
Do not scale; work to figured dimensions only.
P18 2026-10-07 scheme A adopted: serpentine balcony on every plan; site named
P19 2026-10-07 serpentine waist deepened 0.75 to 1.35 m; 15.7 m² of balcony a floor
P20 2026-10-07 internal partitions 100 mm red brick, specified by the client
P21 2026-10-07 300 mm external and party walls: brick, colour unrestricted
